title_zh: 后美联储时代的分化 | Jeffrey Rosenberg（BlackRock）、Bryant Bankronkite（AllSpring）
subtitle_zh: AI 成为主导变量：收益率、信用与股债关系在美联储按兵不动后如何重定价。

turns.en: ETF Edge is sponsored by State Street Investment Management. Getting there starts here. Welcome to ETF Edge, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange-traded funds, you're in the right place.
turns.zh: 《ETF Edge》由 State Street Investment Management 赞助播出。抵达目标，从这里开始。欢迎收听《ETF Edge》播客。如果你想了解关于交易所交易基金（ETF）的最新洞见，那你可算来对地方了。

turns.en: Every week, we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis, and breaking down what it all means for investors. I'm your host, Dominic Chu.
turns.zh: 每周我们都会为你带来精彩的访谈、深入的市场分析，并为大家拆解这一切对投资者究竟意味着什么。我是你们的主持人 Dominic Chu。

turns.en: Though the Fed elected to stand still on rates, certain parts of the fixed income and equities markets are on the move in response. Here is my conversation with Jeffrey Rosenberg, Senior Portfolio Manager of BlackRock's Systematic Alternatives ETF, alongside Bryant-Bankronkite, Senior Portfolio Manager for All Spring Global Investments.
turns.zh: 尽管这次美联储决定在利率上按兵不动，但固定收益和股票市场的某些板块已经率先动了起来。下面是我与 BlackRock 系统化替代方案 ETF（Systematic Alternatives ETF）高级组合经理 Jeffrey Rosenberg，以及 AllSpring Global Investments 高级组合经理 Bryant Bankronkite 的对谈。

turns.en: I had mentioned a couple of the things in our intro with regard to the Fed and yields. But overall, this market has been one that's been very bumpy for a lot of investors across many different asset classes.
turns.zh: 我在开场里提到了几件事，关于美联储和收益率。但总体而言，这轮行情对很多横跨不同资产类别的投资者来说都非常颠簸。

turns.en: And perhaps that leads us to start maybe with you, Jeffrey, about this. I wonder what your take is from a portfolio manager's standpoint about just what kinds of factors are driving the most of the market narrative in your mind these days.
turns.zh: 也许我们就从你开始吧，Jeffrey。我很好奇，从一个组合经理的角度看，在你心里，如今究竟是哪些因素在主导市场的叙事。

turns.en: Yeah, Dom, I think just to pick up on yesterday's conversation with the Fed share, I found the most interesting interchanges around his characterization of financial conditions.
turns.zh: 好的，Dom，我想接着昨天关于美联储的那场对话往下说。我觉得最有意思的，是围绕他对金融条件（financial conditions）的那番描述。

turns.en: He had this conversation with one of the reporters where he started to talk about the questions came in around oil and what was the impact of the rise in oil.
turns.zh: 他和一位记者有这样一段对话，问题问到了油价，问油价上涨的影响是什么。

turns.en: And he started to talk about how Treasury yields had had this amazing correlation with oil. And then in October, it just stopped. And then he went on to say, I don't write a Wall Street newsletter, so I'm not going to comment on that.
turns.zh: 他开始谈到，美国国债收益率曾和油价有着惊人的相关性，可到了十月，这种关系突然就断了。接着他还说，我又不写华尔街的简报，所以我不想对这个发表评论。

turns.en: Well, I don't write a Wall Street newsletter either, but I do run iShow Systematic Alternative Active ETF, and we want to talk to our clients about what's going on in the portfolios.
turns.zh: 我确实也不写华尔街的简报，但我经营着 IALT——系统化替代主动管理 ETF（Systematic Alternatives Active ETF），我们是要跟客户讲清楚组合里到底在发生什么的。

turns.en: And so what he didn't talk about was something that I think was the most important takeaway. The correlation between Treasury yields and oil, 80% this year, that's outsized relative to normal kinds of correlations.
turns.zh: 他没说的是——我觉得那才是最重要的启示。今年以来国债收益率和油价的相关性高达 80%，相对于正常的水平而言，这是极高的。

turns.en: We've basically been trading off of oil for good reason. It's the inflation. It's the downstream impact. Oil reached new highs in October, over 115, and Treasury yields went down.
turns.zh: 基本上我们一直在跟着油价走，这有充分的理由：是通胀，是它带来的下游影响。油价在十月创下新高，超过了 115，而国债收益率反而往下走了。

turns.en: So it told us something really important, that in the market's mind, the geopolitical risk is secondary to the AI risk. And what happened in October is we've had a little bit of an AI retracement, and yields went lower because an AI retracement writ large is an economic retracement.
turns.zh: 这说明了一件非常重要的事：在大家心里，地缘政治风险是次于 AI 风险的。而十月发生的事情是，我们经历了一点点 AI 的回调，收益率因此走低，因为一场大范围的（writ large）AI 回调，其实就是一场经济的回调。

turns.en: It's a little bit of what you're seeing in the GDP report today. AI is everything, everywhere, all of the time, and that growth is being held up by AI, both on the investment side and through the wealth effect, the consumption side.
turns.zh: 这跟你今天在 GDP 报告里看到的情况也有点像。AI 无处不在、无时不在，而当下的经济增长是靠 AI 撑着的——既撑投资端，也通过财富效应撑消费端。

turns.en: And what that means is if you have a wobble, it's a growth impact, it's a disinflationary impact. And the only thing that hedges your portfolio in that environment, the thing that everybody wants to hate, loves to hate, ourselves included, the long end of the Treasury curve.
turns.zh: 这意味着，一旦出现一点颠簸，那就是增长冲击，也是去通胀（disinflationary）的冲击。而在那种环境下唯一能对冲你组合的东西——也就是人人都爱去恨的那样东西，我们自己也不例外——就是国债曲线的长端。

turns.en: So I thought that was a really interesting interchange. She didn't take it all the way, but it's a really important lesson that we should take away from this last month of market performance.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得那是一段非常有意思的对话。他没把话说透，但这是我们从上个月的市场表现里应该汲取的一个非常重要的教训。

turns.en: Okay, Jeff, let me follow up with you on that one there, because for the longest time, we had talked about this idea that Treasuries have traditionally been a safe haven in times of geopolitical conflict, in times of economic distress.
turns.zh: 好的，Jeff，我想就这一点追问你。因为很长时间以来，我们一直在讲一个理念：国债历来是地缘政治冲突、经济动荡时的避风港。

turns.en: If you were worried about the economy in the future, you thought things were going to go down, you bought Treasuries because they were the more attractive asset to hold.
turns.zh: 如果你担心未来的经济，觉得情况会转差，你会去买国债，因为它是更具吸引力的持有资产。

turns.en: That was not the case over the course of the past six to nine months when we saw yields rise the way that they did. Does this in your mind signal for you a return to, I mean, I don't know what's normal these days, but more traditional market constructs of the relationship between stocks and bonds?
turns.zh: 过去六到九个月里收益率那样上行的时候，情况却不是这样。在你看来，这是否意味着——我也不知道现在什么才算正常了——市场回到了股票和债券关系那种更传统的结构？

turns.en: So it's really a nuanced kind of answer here, and unfortunately, the simple answer is no. It's not a return to normal where normal was bonds, hedge stocks, and we have great confidence in that, and just understand why, because these are the conflicting forces on bonds.
turns.zh: 所以这个问题的答案其实很微妙，而遗憾的是，简单的回答是：不是。它并没有回到所谓‘债券对冲股票、我们对此充满信心’的那种常态。你得理解为什么，因为债券身上这几股力量是互相冲突的。

turns.en: The oil price increases, the persistent rise of, or not the rise, but the level of inflation above target that Warsh talked about yesterday.
turns.zh: 油价的上涨、Warsh 昨天提到的通胀持续高企——不是通胀的上升，而是通胀的水平高于目标。

turns.en: These are challenges to fixed income, and it's a challenge to the efficacy of fixed income as a hedge because we have too much inflation, so that limits the ability of the Fed to provide accommodation when inflation is above target.
turns.zh: 这些都是固定收益面临的挑战，也是对固定收益作为对冲工具有效性的挑战，因为通胀太高了，这就限制了美联储在通胀高于目标时提供宽松的能力。

turns.en: So that part we haven't gotten away from. What I think we learned in the last month is that if it's big enough, if the AI trend returns against the macroeconomic and inflationary trends, it can bring about a wholesale change in that direction.
turns.zh: 所以那一块我们并没有摆脱。我觉得过去这一个月学到的是：如果 AI 这股趋势足够强，压过了宏观和通胀趋势，它就能让那个方向发生整体性的转变。

turns.en: That's disinflationary, and bonds may react, as they did in the month of October, positively to that. So there is some diversification benefit to be recognized there, but it's not going to be one directional, and it's not going to be without a cost.
turns.zh: 那种转变是去通胀的，债券可能会像十月那样对它有正面反应。所以这里面确实存在一些分散化的好处，但它不会是单向的，也不会是没有代价的。

turns.en: The cost is, if you're outside of that tail probability scenario of AI unraveling the economy, and you're in the more core scenario that this has got a lot longer to play out, then bonds are going to be challenged by that core scenario, rising inflation, rising term premium, the fiscal challenges, everything that we talk about.
turns.zh: 这个代价就是：如果你不在‘AI 拖垮经济’这个尾部概率情景里，而是在那个更核心的情景——也就是这一切还会持续更久——里，那债券就会被这个核心情景所挑战：通胀上行、期限溢价上行、财政挑战，所有这些我们一直在讨论的东西。

turns.en: It highlights, I think, another part of this conversation, which is the investor's needs for alternative forms of diversification. I mentioned IALT, a fund that I run.
turns.zh: 这也凸显了这场对话的另一个部分，就是投资者对另类分散化方式的需求。我提到了 IALT，我管理的那只基金。

turns.en: This is bringing hedge fund type strategies to the massives through an ETF wrap or something. No one has ever seen and no one has ever done before what we're doing in this fund.
turns.zh: 它做的事情，是通过 ETF 的外壳把类似对冲基金的策略带给大众，这是以前从没人见过、也从未有人做过的事。

turns.en: It's about using alpha as a diversifier, because you have just a lot of beta in your portfolios. On the equities side, that beta is good. It's been the beneficiary from the AI tech trade, but you have the challenge of a lot of concentration in that.
turns.zh: 核心是用 alpha 来做分散化，因为你的组合里 beta 已经太多了。股票这边，这个 beta 是好事，它是 AI 科技行情的受益者，但你面临的挑战是里面的集中度太高。

turns.en: How do investors deal with that? Well, diversifier, diversifiers, and fixed income isn't the perfect solution here. You want to think about, how can I diversify my equity portfolio?
turns.zh: 投资者该怎么应对？那就是分散化工具、分散化工具。而固定收益在这里并不是完美的答案。你要想的是：我怎么才能给自己的股票组合做分散化？

turns.en: By adding some alpha, which is what we do in IALT, can be one of those solutions. Interesting as well, because that's the alternatives perspective, the fixed income perspective.
turns.zh: 通过加入一些 alpha——这正是我们在 IALT 里做的事——可以是解决方案之一。也挺有意思，因为这是替代方案的视角、固定收益的视角。

turns.en: Brian, I'll turn to you for this one here, because you handle more of the straight-up equity side of the equation for all-spring with regard to your portfolios and their exposure.
turns.zh: Brian，这个话题我想转到你这边，因为在 AllSpring，你更多是负责纯股票这一块，管着你们组合和它们的敞口。

turns.en: I wonder, to Jeffrey's original point here, what was your key takeaway as you listened to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh during his press conference and comments yesterday vis-a-vis how you think equity markets are shaping up right now, given that backdrop that we're seeing on a macro big picture basis.
turns.zh: 我想问问，呼应 Jeffrey 最初提到的那一点，当你昨天听美联储主席 Kevin Warsh 的记者会和讲话时，你最主要的收获是什么？在我们看到的这个宏观大背景下，你怎么看股票市场正在成形的方式。

turns.en: It seems like investors' concern around what Chair Warsh was saying was really what he didn't say. There's also more about the reaction function.
turns.zh: 看起来，投资者对 Warsh 主席讲话的担忧，其实更多在于他没说的那些话。还有关于他的反应函数（reaction function）。

turns.en: They want to know thresholds at which point the committee will begin to act, how fast they're going to act. He's chosen to say nothing about those things, and so the market's worried about that.
turns.zh: 他们想知道委员会将在什么阈值开始行动、行动会有多快。他选择对这些只字不提，所以市场对此很担心。

turns.en: I did hear two things that I thought were important to keep in mind. One, he did show some resolve around wanting to fight inflation. There will be a reaction, it seems like, but we're not ready yet to say when that's going to happen.
turns.zh: 我倒是听到两点我认为很重要的。第一，他确实展现了一定决心，想对抗通胀。看起来会有反应，只是我们还没到能断言那何时发生的时候。

turns.en: That's one thing. The other thing I thought that was really interesting and fairly astute in the way he said it is that the rising rate environment is working its way into the cracks of the economy.
turns.zh: 这是一点。另一点我觉得很有意思，也说得相当犀利：加息的环境正在渗透进经济的缝隙里。

turns.en: It's happening slowly, but it's happening in really profound ways. As you look closely at equity, as you can see, it's starting to unfold. There's three ways I see it happening.
turns.zh: 它来得很慢，但正在以非常深刻的方式发生。你只要仔细看股票市场，正如你所见，它开始显现了。我看到有三个渠道。

turns.en: Number one, it's changing demand. You think about the demand for certain products or certain services, and I put housing at the epicenter of that.
turns.zh: 第一，它正在改变需求。想想对某些产品、某些服务的需求，我认为房地产是这场冲击的中心。

turns.en: As rates have moved higher, we're seeing pressure on demand for housing and housing affordability. What is impacting the economy? It used to be said that housing is the economy and the economy is housing.
turns.zh: 随着利率走高，我们看到住房需求和住房可负担性都承受压力。以前人们常说，房地产就是经济，经济就是房地产。

turns.en: Now, AI is the economy and the economy is AI, but we're seeing that work its way into the cracks of the housing market. The second thing we're seeing is it's working its way into the cracks of financing.
turns.zh: 现在，AI 就是经济，经济就是 AI，但我们看到这股冲击正在渗透进房地产市场的缝隙。第二件事，是它正在渗透进融资的缝隙。

turns.en: When money was cheap, every business, no matter how good the asset base was, no how competitively the advantage it was, it had access to capital.
turns.zh: 当资金便宜的时候，每一家企业——不管它的资产基础有多好、竞争优势有多强——都能拿到资本。

turns.en: They kept a lot of companies actually in the private markets longer than maybe they should have. As rates rise, we're starting to see the companies that deserve the capital from those that don't.
turns.zh: 这让很多公司在私募市场里待的时间，可能比它们本该待的还要长。随着利率上升，我们开始把配得上资本的公司和配不上的区分开来。

turns.en: You're seeing the projects that deserve the capital from those that don't. I put the AI spend, the hyperscalers versus the neoclouds, right in that net epicenter.
turns.zh: 你开始看到哪些项目配得上资本、哪些不配。我认为 AI 的支出——超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers）对新云（neoclouds）——就正好处于这场筛选的中心。

turns.en: We're seeing how it can impact companies differently. The third and final thing that I look at right now is the way change in rates is into the cracks of duration.
turns.zh: 我们看到它对不同公司的影响截然不同。我目前关注的第三、也是最后一点，是利率变化正在渗透进久期（duration）的缝隙。

turns.en: I know we talk about duration on the bond side, and that's more Jeff's world, but in my world, we see it too. Think about how it impacts the valuation of equities, and the longer the duration of the cash flow stream, the more the impact of rising rates negatively impacts the value of the stock.
turns.zh: 我知道我们在债券端老谈久期，那是 Jeff 的领域，但在我的世界里也能看到。想想它怎么影响股票的估值：现金流存续的久期越长，加息对股票估值的负面冲击就越大。

turns.en: Software companies are the key poster child for long duration cash flow streams. It's coming through the cracks. It's not seeping through in a massive way.
turns.zh: 软件公司是长久期现金流最典型的代表。它正在从缝隙里渗进来，还没有大规模地渗透。

turns.en: It's not flooding in yet, but it's working its way in, and that's giving us chances to put capital to work in different areas of the market right now.
turns.zh: 它还没汹涌而入，但正在逐步渗入，这就给了我们当下把资本投到市场不同领域的机会。

turns.en: Brian, okay, I want to follow up there as well, because one of the things about rising rates, the way that we've seen them, is to your point, it does affect the way capital flows around.
turns.zh: Brian，好的，我也想顺着这个追问一下，因为关于加息、关于我们所看到的这种加息方式，正如你所说，它确实会改变资本流动的方式。

turns.en: It does kind of get you to a point where you have to kind of really pick and choose the types of projects that you green light, the types of investments that you make, because the hurdle rates, those required rates of return are now higher across the board, because the risk-free rates that you get in treasuries are now higher across the board.
turns.zh: 它会把你逼到一个境地：你必须真正精挑细选要放行哪些项目、做哪些投资，因为门槛收益率——那些要求的回报率——现在全面提高了，因为你在国债里拿到的无风险利率现在也全面提高了。

turns.en: Where exactly are those valuation gaps really starting to manifest themselves outside to your point of, say, neoclouds and hyperscalers and some of the straight up AI trade?
turns.zh: 除了你刚才说的新云、超大规模云厂商、以及一些纯 AI 交易之外，这些估值差距到底在哪里开始真正显现出来？

turns.en: Yeah, I think that's right. You have a higher risk-free rate, and that you also are starting to see some differentiation in the credit spread.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得没错。你的无风险利率更高了，同时你也开始看到信用利差上出现一些分化。

turns.en: The caliber of the quality of your cash flow stream, the certainty of your cash flow stream is determining the spread over that treasury. There's some companies that are showing those are blowing out meaningfully, and it's putting pressure on the equities.
turns.zh: 你现金流的质量、现金流的确定性，正在决定相对于国债的利差。有些公司显示它们的利差在大幅走阔，这给它们的股票带来了压力。

turns.en: And so we talked about the hyperscalers as an example of that. You're looking at it also, though, from how our banks respond to these. So banks aren't having a financing issue, but the more rates move certain asset-sensitive banks versus liability-sensitive banks are beginning to diverge from each other.
turns.zh: 我们拿超大规模云厂商作为一个例子。但你也要看我们的银行如何对这类变化做出反应。银行本身没有融资问题，但随着利率移动，资产敏感型银行和负债敏感型银行开始彼此分化。

turns.en: And we're seeing it in the real economy. People are making hard choices because affordability is going up. So the affordability of homes, the affordability of cars, and all of that cascades through the construction markets, et cetera.
turns.zh: 我们在实体经济里也看到了这一点。人们在做艰难的选择，因为负担压力越来越大——房子买不起、车也买不起，而这一切会一路传导到建筑市场等等。

turns.en: So it's working its way into the real economy. And what I like about this is that we're starting to see the good ideas rise to the top and you're seeing the bad ideas begin to fall apart.
turns.zh: 所以它正在渗透进实体经济。我喜欢的一点是，我们开始看到好的想法浮上水面，坏的想法开始崩塌。

turns.en: It's been very challenging in the equity markets to find differentiation. Things have moved in lumps. And I think ETFs, frankly, have allowed investors to do that.
turns.zh: 在股票市场里，想找到差异化其实一直非常困难，很多东西都是整块整块地一起动的。而我觉得，坦率说，ETF 让投资者得以做到这一点。

turns.en: We have so many thematic ETFs that people push into categories. The All-Spring Special Large-Cat Value ETF, ASLV, is a diversified ETF across different sectors and industries where we can participate in all of these unique areas of opportunities.
turns.zh: 我们有太多主题型 ETF，人们把它们归到各种类别里。AllSpring 的这只 ASLV（All-Spring Special Large-Cap Value ETF），是一只跨越不同板块和行业的分散化 ETF，我们可以在所有这些独特的机会领域里参与其中。

turns.en: But it really is about single-stock selection and alpha opportunity that's generated because people are thinking too thematically, thinking too macro at times.
turns.zh: 但这真的在于个股选择，以及由此产生的 alpha 机会——因为人们有时想得太过主题化、太过宏观化了。

turns.en: Jeff, let's talk about the alpha that you can find, especially for a product like yours. If you talk about systematic investments, especially when it comes to fixed income and other alternative investments, you've now put iAlt and those hedge fund type strategies that you alluded to before in an ETF wrapper, making them a little bit more accessible and easy to kind of comprehend for investors who are trying to get into a product that can
turns.zh: Jeff，我们来聊聊你能找到的 alpha，尤其像你产品这样的。谈到系统化投资，特别是固定收益和其他另类投资方面，你们现在把 IALT 以及你之前提到的那些对冲基金式的策略放进了 ETF 的外壳里，让那些想要买入一只既能分散化、又能带来超额收益产品的投资者，更容易上手、更容易理解。

turns.en: be a diversifier while still adding out performance. So if you have a mandate that can allow you to go different places, what exactly have you seen about the opportunities where you are kind of putting money to work, so to speak, in some of that iAlt strategy?
turns.zh: 在起到分散化作用的同时，仍能带来超额表现。所以如果你的授权允许你去不同的地方，那么在 IALT 策略里，你具体在哪些地方把钱投出去、把资金真正用起来了？

turns.en: Yeah. I want to also, I'll just contrast a little bit with what Brian said. In iAlt, we do this across the capital stacks. We do it in equities.
turns.zh: 好的。我也想稍微对照一下 Brian 说的。在 IALT 里，我们横跨整个资本结构来做这件事，我们在股票里做。

turns.en: We do it across macro markets. And so one of the things I'll disagree with Brian a little bit on is that this is a market that has been really characterized by winners and losers.
turns.zh: 我们也在宏观市场里做。所以我和 Brian 有一点小分歧：我认为这个市场其实一直是赢家通吃、输家出局。

turns.en: It's driven by the AI theme. The AI theme is a wedge. If you're on the wrong side of the AI technology revolution, your stock and its prospects are suffering.
turns.zh: 它是由 AI 主题驱动的。AI 主题就像一把楔子。如果你站错了 AI 技术革命的那一边，你的股票及其前景都在受煎熬。

turns.en: If you're on the winning side of it, you're thriving. And that divergence in fortunes is creating a very, very fruitful opportunity set for the types of strategies that we employ in iAlt.
turns.zh: 如果你站在它赢的那一边，你就在蓬勃发展。这种命运的分化，正是为我们 IALT 里采用的那类策略创造了极其、极其丰厚的机会。

turns.en: And that strategy is long, short market neutral. So we can find opportunities on the long side, but we can also find opportunities on the short side.
turns.zh: 那个策略是多头、空头、市场中性。所以我们既能在多头端找到机会，也能在空头端找到机会。

turns.en: That's the unique innovation that we're bringing to this portfolio, to the ETF wrapper that just doesn't exist. I mean, BlackRock, we pioneered market access, beta, cheap beta, beta is plentiful, it should be cheap, IVV, three basis points.
turns.zh: 这就是我们带给这个组合、带进这个 ETF 外壳的独特创新，别处根本没有。我是说，BlackRock 是市场通道（market access）的开创者——我们主打便宜的 beta：beta 是充裕的，理应便宜，比如 IVV，三个基点。

turns.en: Alpha investing is something completely different. It's a little bit challenging. It's new. We've been doing it on the institutional side for a generation.
turns.zh: 但 alpha 投资完全是另一回事。它有点难，也很新。我们在机构端已经做了整整一代人了。

turns.en: Deep retail investors have never really had access to these types of investment strategies. And so when you bring in the short side capability, you open up a world of investment opportunities.
turns.zh: 深度的零售投资者其实从来没有真正接触过这类投资策略。所以当你把空头这一侧的能力带进来，你就打开了一整个投资机会的世界。

turns.en: And that world today is very, very plentiful because you have so much dispersion going on. And that dispersion, as I was mentioning, we do it in the micro side, but you also see it on the macro side because AI, again, is a driver of differentiation.
turns.zh: 而今天那个世界极其、极其丰富，因为现在有太多的分化（dispersion）在发生。就像我说的，我们做分化是在微观层面，但你在宏观层面也能看到它，因为说到底 AI 又是那个制造差异化的推手。

turns.en: And the more differentiation that you're having across both macro and micro markets, the greater the opportunities. And here's really the important part, is that fund can deliver returns without the beta and the factor exposures.
turns.zh: 在宏观和微观市场里，分化越大，机会就越多。而真正关键的部分是：这只基金能在不依赖 beta 和因子敞口的情况下创造回报。

turns.en: So you get diversification from what you already have too much exposure to in your portfolios, which is the concentration of the AI winners, the concentration that we see within portfolios.
turns.zh: 所以你能从你组合里已经敞口过大的东西上获得分散化——也就是 AI 赢家股的集中、我们在各个组合里看到的那种集中度。

turns.en: Without that tool of being able to open up the capacity to reduce exposures through short shorting, you really end up with portfolios that are overly concentrated to the winners in the market because most of what portfolios attract are market cap weighted exposures.
turns.zh: 如果没有通过做空来降低敞口这个工具，最终你的组合就会过度集中在市场的赢家上，因为大多数组合吸引来的都是市值加权的敞口。

turns.en: Even if I can kind of do some active management around it, we see it's highly limited. Often it's structurally limited because portfolios have mandated diversification requirements.
turns.zh: 即便我能在它周围做一些主动管理，我们也看到那非常受限。很多时候它是结构性受限的，因为组合有强制的分散化要求。

turns.en: The big reason why active equity investors have really, you know, lagged their benchmark because the concentration of portfolios makes it so hard to find active risk without taking underweights to the big winners.
turns.zh: 主动型股票投资者之所以大幅跑输基准，一个很大的原因就在于组合的集中度过高，让你很难在不承担对大赢家低配的情况下找到主动风险。

turns.en: And the big winners have been AI and technology. So what you get in IALT is just something you've never seen before. And it's so important today and it's so fruitful in terms of the opportunity set for adding additional sources of returns.
turns.zh: 而大赢家一直是 AI 和科技。所以你在 IALT 里得到的，是一种你从未见过的东西。在今天，它如此重要，在提供额外回报来源的机会层面如此丰厚。

turns.en: Just really quickly, Jeff, what exactly have you seen? Where have you seen the best opportunities for short and or long positions here? Is it more prevalent in the currency and rates markets?
turns.zh: 简单问一下，Jeff，你具体看到了什么？你在哪里看到了最好的空头和/或多头机会？这些机会是更多存在于外汇和利率市场吗？

turns.en: Is it more prevalent in certain commodities markets? Is it more prevalent in fixed income or equities? How is that kind of analysis? Because you do run an actively managed fund.
turns.zh: 还是更多存在于某些大宗商品市场？是更多在固定收益还是股票里？这类分析是怎么做的？因为你确实管理的是一只主动型基金。

turns.en: How is that kind of shaken out and where do you see some of those notable convergences and divergences? Well, a couple of things. One is we have more of a strategic approach to allocating our risk across the buckets of opportunity.
turns.zh: 那这种分析最终怎么落定，你又在哪些地方看到了那些值得关注的趋同和分化？好的，有那么几点。首先，我们在各个机会板块之间配置风险时，采取的是更偏战略性的方法。

turns.en: And so when you think about opportunities in the FX space, in the cross currency interest rate space, in the commodity space, that will occupy a portion of our funds risk.
turns.zh: 所以当你想到外汇领域、跨币种利率领域、大宗商品领域的机会时，这些会占据我们基金风险的一部分。

turns.en: And then think about, so think about as that is the kind of the top down opportunity set. And then you think about the bottoms up opportunity set.
turns.zh: 然后，你把这一块看作自上而下的机会集。接下来你再想自下而上的机会集。

turns.en: That's really inside the equity market. So thinking about the differences between growth and value and factor exposures, trying to neutralize the generic factor exposure and isolate the real pure idiosyncratic exposures.
turns.zh: 那其实就在股票市场内部。也就是思考成长和价值之间的差异、因子敞口的差异，尽量中和掉那些通用的因子敞口，把真正纯粹的特质（idiosyncratic）敞口给隔离出来。

turns.en: And that's where we've seen a tremendous amount of opportunity. Interesting thing, Dom, is it's been an incredibly strong environment for both macro orientations of alpha and these micro orientations of alpha.
turns.zh: 而那正是我们看到巨量机会的地方。有意思的是，Dom，无论是对宏观取向的 alpha，还是对这些微观取向的 alpha，这都是一个异常强劲的环境。

turns.en: And I think a lot of that has to do with the downstream effects of the AI theme. It's not only the AI theme, we have other themes as well, like the geopolitical risk.
turns.zh: 我觉得这在很大程度上跟 AI 主题的下游效应有关。不只是 AI 主题，我们还有别的主线，比如地缘政治风险。

turns.en: We had a reflation theme in the market that was very powerful driver of some of the macro alphas that we express in the fund. But you also have that at the same time happening as very strong, powerful sources of alpha at the idiosyncratic space.
turns.zh: 市场里有过一波再通胀（reflation）主题，它是我们基金所表达的某些宏观 alpha 的非常强劲的推手。但与此同时，同样的这些力量在个股特质层面，也在成为非常强劲、非常有力的 alpha 来源。

turns.en: And the combination has been this very unique environment, very strong environment for alpha oriented returns. It's interesting, Bryant, because what Jeffrey describes is pretty much fruitful ground for a stock picker or somebody who's looking for those micro nuances among assets within the equity sphere.
turns.zh: 两相叠加，就造成了一个非常独特的环境，一个对 alpha 导向回报极其强劲的环境。这很有意思，Bryant，因为 Jeffrey 描述的这些，几乎正是选股者、或者寻找股票内部那些资产间微妙差异的人的沃土。

turns.en: So I guess on that line, Bryant, if you are able to be a stock picker, what types of things are you looking for for where that next leg of outperformance is going to come from?
turns.zh: 所以顺着这个思路，Bryant，如果你能做一个选股者，你正在寻找什么样的东西，来判断下一波超额表现会从哪里来？

turns.en: Are there certain factors, characteristics, certain themes that you think are going to play out as opportunistic for the, say, next six to 12 months?
turns.zh: 有没有某些因子、某些特征、某些主题，你认为在未来比如说六到十二个月里会演变成机会？

turns.en: Yeah, there's three basic building blocks that we think set up any company for success. And without them, you likely aren't going to have long term success as a business.
turns.zh: 有的，我们认为让任何一家公司具备成功潜力的，有三个基本构件。缺了它们，你作为一家企业很可能不会有长期的成功。

turns.en: So number one, we need to identify some unique competitive advantage. What asset base does a company have that creates a unique edge that allows customers the need to use them?
turns.zh: 第一，我们需要识别出某种独特的竞争优势。一家公司拥有怎样的资产基础，能创造出一种独特的优势，让客户不得不使用它？

turns.en: And can they maintain that asset base and invest in that asset base over time? Number two, that asset base should show a propensity to throw off a lots of free cash flow.
turns.zh: 他们能不能维护这份资产基础，并持续在其上投资？第二，这份资产基础应该展现出产生大量自由现金流的倾向。

turns.en: We like low capital intensity, all is equal. We like high free cash flow margins. And so that cash flow becomes the fuel that feeds into number three, which is a strong balance sheet.
turns.zh: 在其他条件相同的情况下，我们喜欢低资本密集度，喜欢高的自由现金流利润率。于是这份现金流就成了燃料，喂给第三点——强劲的资产负债表。

turns.en: Ultimately, how a company uses their capital is the only thing they control. We can talk about the Fed and interest rates or GDP or broader economic issues, but company management teams control how they use their capital.
turns.zh: 归根到底，一家公司如何使用它的资本，是唯一真正由它自己掌控的事。我们可以聊美联储、聊利率、聊 GDP、聊更大的经济问题，但公司管理层掌控的是他们如何使用资本。

turns.en: But in order to do that, you have to have availability of capital, get to have financial freedom. So all of our businesses, all of our companies have tremendous financial freedom to invest in their future.
turns.zh: 但要做到这一点，你必须要有资本的可用性和充裕度，要有财务自由。所以我们所有的生意、所有的公司，都有巨大的财务自由去投资于它们的未来。

turns.en: And so where we find opportunity today is in places like technology. We think the CapEx spend by Google, Google having a tough day-to-day after earnings, obviously, but we think the money they're spending is showing high returns.
turns.zh: 所以我们今天在像科技这样的地方找到了机会。我们认为 Google 的资本开支（CapEx）——Google 财报后日子显然不好过——但我们认为它们投入的钱正在展现出很高的回报。

turns.en: We believe that they're willing to disrupt themselves to create a much bigger, better, more dominant asset base in the future that will have even better free cash flow profiles in the future.
turns.zh: 我们相信它们愿意颠覆自己，以在未来创造一个更庞大、更好、更具主导地位的资产基础，届时会有更好的自由现金流结构。

turns.en: So technology, we think is a great place right now. We also think healthcare is really interesting. Demographics are on your side. And all the new drugs that are currently hitting the market is allowing us to expand the duration of life cycles.
turns.zh: 所以科技，我们认为现在是个很好的地方。我们也认为医疗保健真的很有意思。人口结构站在你这一边，而当前上市的所有新药，让我们得以延展生命周期的久期。

turns.en: We think it's going to get even bigger over time. So a name like LabCorp, where they do diagnostic tests, blood, skin testing. We're going to need a lot more of that.
turns.zh: 我们认为它会随时间变得更大。所以像 LabCorp 这样的名字，它们做诊断检测——血液、皮肤检测。我们会需要越来越多这样的服务。

turns.en: And that's critical to not only our long-term health, which is maintenance, but also the customization of medicine. So LabCorp is using their capital for R&D, for acquisitions to expand on that asset base.
turns.zh: 这不仅对我们长期的健康——也就是维持性医疗——至关重要，对医疗的个性化也至关重要。所以 LabCorp 正把资本用在研发、用在收购上，去扩展它的资产基础。

turns.en: And maybe one final place that we're seeing opportunity right now is in industrials, very broad sector. But when you narrow down, aerospace and defense is a category that we think is showing structural opportunity.
turns.zh: 也许我们当下看到机会的最后一个领域是工业——一个非常宽泛的板块。但当你聚焦下来，航空航天与防务是一个我们认为正展现出结构性机会的类别。

turns.en: Not cyclical, but true structural opportunity where the commercial aerospace ramp up is happening, but the aftermarket tail is so long and so supportive of consistent free cash flow.
turns.zh: 不是周期性的，而是真正的结构性机会：商业航空的爬坡正在发生，而售后市场（aftermarket）这条尾巴又长又稳，非常支撑持续的自由现金流。

turns.en: And the re-arming of the world, hate to have it happening, but the reality is America and NATO overall is going to be rebuilding their munitions.
turns.zh: 还有世界的重新武装——不愿看到它发生，但现实是美国和整个北约都在重建它们的弹药储备。

turns.en: And so defense spending in names like Raytheon, for example, who has both aero and defense, we think it's an opportunity for the company to grow that competitive edge and that cash flow.
turns.zh: 所以在防务开支上，像 Raytheon 这样兼具航空和防务业务的名字，我们认为这是一个让公司壮大其竞争优势和现金流的机会。

turns.en: So opportunities everywhere. So Stop Pickers market finally, in my opinion, and we're taking advantage of it. Interesting. So alphabet on one hand, then you've got RTX on the other hand, and then LabCorp, a little bit more healthcare defensive for sure there.
turns.zh: 所以机会遍地。所以在我看来，这终于成了一个选股者的市场，而我们正在利用它。有意思，一边是 Alphabet，另一边是 RTX，还有 LabCorp——那一个肯定更偏医疗保健的防御属性。

turns.en: Jeff, I'm going to give the last word to you here. Where are you seeing those opportunities akin to kind of what we heard from Bryant there?
turns.zh: Jeff，最后一段发言我想留给你。在听到 Bryant 刚才说的那些之后，你又在哪些地方看到类似的机会？

turns.en: There have been sell-offs in places like the Treasury complex in investment grade, right? Because it's more tied to spreads over Treasury products, even in places like High Yield that are structurally a little bit more tied to risk aversion and risk appetite in addition to rates as well.
turns.zh: 在像投资级里的国债板块这样的地方出现过抛售，对吧？因为它更紧密地挂钩于国债产品之上的利差，甚至在高收益债这样、在结构上除了利率之外还更挂钩于风险规避与风险偏好的地方，也是如此。

turns.en: Even private credit has been a place where people are looking. So how exactly do you see all of those opportunities shaping up and how do you handicap them?
turns.zh: 甚至私募信贷（private credit）也成了人们关注的地方。所以你到底怎么看这些机会的成形，又怎么去权衡它们？

turns.en: Yeah. Bryant mentioned it as well. On the credit side, there's been a pretty decent repricing, triple C's have been repricing all year long.
turns.zh: 是的，Bryant 也提到了。在信用这边，已经出现了一次相当可观的重新定价，三级债（triple C's）一整年都在重新定价。

turns.en: So we're starting to see some better differentiation in terms of credit and credit availability. I think the biggest opportunity though is still in the quality space and in the kind of the mid-front end part of the curve.
turns.zh: 所以我们开始看到信用和信用可得性上更好的分化。不过我认为最大的机会仍然在高质量（quality）这一块，以及在曲线中段偏前端的那一部分。

turns.en: While we've had a widening, we are still on the tight end of credit spreads. What's happening, there's a little, it's not little, it's pretty big theme around AI again and Hyperscale as we got Microsoft in the markets today, pushing out a very large deal.
turns.zh: 虽然经历了利差走阔，我们仍处于信用利差的偏紧一端。正在发生的是——这不是小事，而是相当大的主题——又是 AI 和超大规模，因为今天我们看到 Microsoft 进入市场，推出了一笔非常庞大的发行。

turns.en: There's a lot of debt issuance that is coming down the pipe and it is repricing the bond markets. It's repricing to a better starting point, but it's still a relatively tight spread environment and so that favors a bit more quality exposure where you've really seen the kind of resumption and value in fixed income is by having some term premium come back into the market and that kind of front to middle part of the maturity spectrum is where you see that in quality
turns.zh: 有一大批债务发行正涌来，它正在给债券市场重新定价。它是在向一个更好的起点重新定价，但整体仍是一个相对紧的利差环境，所以这更偏向于多一点高质量的敞口。你在固定收益里真正看到其回归和价值所在的方式，是让一些期限溢价重新回到市场，而那种从前端到中段的久期区间，正是你在高质量利差里看到它的地方。

turns.en: spreads. You're getting the right balance between kind of yield pickup over cash without taking a lot of indirect equity exposure by having too much down in quality in the credit space.
turns.zh: 利差。你在相对现金的收益增强、和不承担太多间接股票敞口之间，取得恰当的平衡——也就是别在信用那边下沉太多质量。

turns.en: I think that is kind of the sweet spot for kind of income and fixed income right now. All right, opportunities on both the credit and the equity side of things.
turns.zh: 我认为这就是当下收益和固定收益领域的甜蜜点。好了，信用和股票两边都有机会。

turns.en: Now it's time to round out the conversation with some thoughtful analysis and perspective to help you better understand ETFs with our Markets 102 portion of the podcast.
turns.zh: 现在，是时候用我们播客的 Market 102 环节，以一些深思熟虑的分析和视角为这场对话收尾，帮你更好地理解 ETF。

turns.en: Jeffrey Rosenberg, Senior Portfolio Manager at BlackRock's Systematic Alternatives ETF, ticker IALT, continues with us now. You know, Jeff, it was a fascinating conversation and one of the things I wanted to kind of pick up on is one of kind of your closing-ish comments during the online show this week and that was just how much we are seeing some of the effects of the debt markets vis-a-vis AI playing out.
turns.zh: BlackRock 系统化替代方案 ETF（代码 IALT）的高级组合经理 Jeffrey Rosenberg 继续和我们在一起。Jeff，这是一场非常精彩的对话，我想接着聊的一点，是你这周在线节目里那段近似收尾的话——我们正看到债务市场相对于 AI 的这些影响有多深。

turns.en: We know that there are concerns in the debt market right now about the issuance, the amount of capital it's going to take to kind of fund this massive AI data center expansion, but there seems to be some pushback from investors and it's playing out in a lot of different parts of the market right now.
turns.zh: 我们知道，债务市场目前对发行、对资助这场大规模 AI 数据中心扩张所需资本的量级存有担忧，但投资者似乎在给出一些阻力，而这股压力此刻正在市场的很多不同部位显现。

turns.en: So I wonder if you could give us your thoughts on expanding on that particular thought. What exactly have you observed about AI and debt issuance that is causing some of this kind of more direct disruption in credit markets?
turns.zh: 所以我想你能不能就这一点展开谈谈。关于 AI 和债务发行，你具体观察到了什么，正在信用市场里引发这种更直接的扰动？

turns.en: Yeah, so it's a really fascinating conversation, but just to put it in its kind of context is just to appreciate where we are in the history of AI and understand that, you know, what we're experiencing today, we had third-quarter GDP and it was blowout and it's all AI related.
turns.zh: 好的，这是一个非常迷人的话题，但要把它放回语境里，你得先明白我们正处于 AI 历史的哪个阶段，并理解——我们今天所经历的：第三季度的 GDP 爆了，而且全都是 AI 相关的。

turns.en: The largest nominal equipment investment since like 1983, 26% growth rate, consumption well above expectations fueled by wealth effect because real income is actually going down.
turns.zh: 这是自 1983 年左右以来最大规模的名义设备投资，增长率达 26%；消费远超预期，由财富效应驱动，因为实际收入其实是在下降的。

turns.en: So where the consumer is getting the oomph to keep spending, they're getting it from their confidence, which is they're getting from the wealth effect.
turns.zh: 所以消费者继续花钱的那股劲，是从他们的信心里来的，而这份信心又是从财富效应里来的。

turns.en: So this AI piece is huge and it's transitioning and the transition occurred in 2026. It's like a chart that I'm putting together for my latest deck called Navigating Investing in an AI World and what the deck shows you is the timeline of a hyperscalar cash flow against capital expenditures.
turns.zh: 所以 AI 这一块是巨大的，而且它正在转型，转型发生在 2026 年。就像我正在为我最新那份名为《Navigating Investing in an AI World》的材料里做的一张图，那张图展示的是一家超大规模云厂商的现金流对资本开支的时间线。

turns.en: And you know, obviously this is coming on the day after a Google's earnings release, which was, you know, a little bit of a bombshell. And really you look at market reaction down 12% last time I looked, it's the biggest one day loss I think ever in Google's history.
turns.zh: 显然，这一切正好发生在 Google 发布财报的第二天，那份财报，怎么说呢，是一记惊雷。你回头看市场的反应，我最后一次看的时候跌了 12%，我想这是 Google 历史上最大的单日跌幅。

turns.en: Note that, that's a really big deal because the market is reacting and what is it reacting to? Well, it's reacting to this shift, right, where the capital expenditure growth rate, second quarter in a row of negative free cash flow for Google, right?
turns.zh: 注意这一点，这非常重要，因为市场正在做出反应，而它在反应什么？它在反应这个转变，对吧——资本开支的增长速度：Google 连续第二个季度自由现金流转负，对吧？

turns.en: And where's that negative free cash flow coming from? It's coming from this rise in capital expenditures. Okay. So that's happening. They're running out or they ran out of internally generated cash flow and now they have to start financing it.
turns.zh: 那这份负自由现金流是从哪来的？来自资本开支的这一路上升。好的，这就是正在发生的事：他们快用尽、或者已经用尽了内部产生的现金流，现在不得不开始去融资了。

turns.en: So the first phases of financing started outside the public bond markets. So when you're outside of the public bond markets, nobody really sees what's going on.
turns.zh: 所以最早的融资阶段是在公开债券市场之外开始的。当你在公开债券市场之外时，其实没人真正看得到在发生什么。

turns.en: I see it, right? Because I participate, but the market broadly, it doesn't see it. The media broadly, it doesn't see it. You don't see the pricing of credit in bank loans.
turns.zh: 我看得到，对吧？因为我参与其中。但整个市场看不到，媒体整体也看不到。你从银行贷款里看不到信用的定价。

turns.en: You don't see it in project finance. You don't see it in private credit because it's private. So okay. So those markets are small. I mean, the bank loan market is big, but the bank's capacity is small.
turns.zh: 你在项目融资里看不到，在私募信贷里也看不到，因为它们是私密的。所以，好，那些市场规模都小。我是说，银行贷款市场很大，但银行的承接能力是有限的。

turns.en: So you run out of capacity very quickly relative to the, what, $4 trillion of estimated capital expenditures over the next four years and everybody's estimate varies, but the estimates are growing.
turns.zh: 所以相对于未来四年大约 4 万亿美元的估计资本开支——每家的估算都不一样，但估算值在不断上升——你的承接能力很快就会耗尽。

turns.en: That's the key thing is like the growth rate of the capital expenditures is increasing. That's what we learned yesterday from Google's earnings and we've been learning from the hyperscalers over the last earnings releases.
turns.zh: 关键在于，资本开支的增长速度本身在加快。这正是我们昨天从 Google 财报里学到的，也是我们从超大规模云厂商过去几次财报里一直学到的。

turns.en: So when the bond markets look at that, they say, oh, where's this all coming? It's coming to me. I'm sorry. The public bond markets, right? Public bond markets are the largest market in the world.
turns.zh: 所以当债券市场看到这些，它们会说：哦，这一切要从哪儿冒出来？是要冒到我这里来。抱歉——是公开的债券市场，对吧？公开债券市场是世界上最大的市场。

turns.en: That's where you can absorb the funding needs and it can be absorbed. I mean, the scale here is still relatively small. These are $40, $50, $60 trillion markets depending on what you put in there globally, relative to $4 trillion of total capital expenditures.
turns.zh: 那里才是你能吸收这些融资需求、并且能够被吸收的地方。我是说，这里的规模相对而言还是小的：这些是 40 万亿、50 万亿、60 万亿美元的市场——取决于你把什么算进去——相对于 4 万亿美元的总资本开支。

turns.en: That's absorbable, but it's a huge marginal issuer and it's increasingly all gonna come and it's gonna come and it's gonna come again and again and again every year.
turns.zh: 这是可以被吸收的，但它是一个巨大的边际发行人，而且越来越多地，它会一波接一波地来，年年如此，一次又一次。

turns.en: So the bond markets are looking at that and they're saying, okay, well, what's the price? What's the clearing price? So I don't think we need to get all like fire and brimstone and sky is falling about the signals that are coming out of the bond markets.
turns.zh: 所以债券市场看着这一切，它们说：好，那价格是多少？清算价格是多少？所以我不觉得我们需要对债券市场传出的信号搞得如临大敌、如天塌下来一般。

turns.en: What we want to interpret those signals properly as a re-pricing of the expectation, an increase of the expectation of issuance into a market that is not unlimited in its capacity.
turns.zh: 我们想要把这些信号正确地解读为一次预期的重新定价——对发行量预期的上调，涌入了一个容量并非无限的市场。

turns.en: It's a very large market and it can absorb it, but when it sees the amount that's coming, it needs to take a higher price to clear that. That's how you bring supply into demand is ultimately at what price will it clear?
turns.zh: 这是一个非常大的市场，它能够吸收，但当它看到要来的量这么大时，它就需要索取更高的价格来清算。你要怎么让供给和需求匹配上，说到底就在于：以什么价格它才能清算？

turns.en: It will clear, but that price may have to be at a lower price, higher yield. When you're seeing this on display today, Microsoft announced a massive $25 billion issuance, surprised to the market, was on the calendar, haven't been back to the bond markets in over a decade or just under a decade, I think 2017 was the last issuance.
turns.zh: 它会清算，但那个价格可能得是更低的债价、更高的收益率。你今天看到的这一幕：Microsoft 宣布了一笔庞大的 250 亿美元发行，让市场吃了一惊——它其实是在日程上的——它们已经十几年没回过债券市场了，或者差不到十年，我想 2017 年是上一次发行。

turns.en: So when they come to market, at least the initial price talk, there's a lot of gamesmanship that goes on in the bond markets around this, but it came very wide to their existing deals.
turns.zh: 所以当它们进入市场，至少是初始的价格指引（price talk），债券市场围绕这个有很多博弈，但它相对于它们现有的债券来得非常之宽。

turns.en: Now that'll probably skinny in like all these do, but Microsoft is like the lowest cost funder within the debt markets. It's TDS trades at 55 basis points, Oracle by contrast trades at 325 basis points, and everyone else is within the large cap IG, they're falling in between.
turns.zh: 现在它大概会像所有这些都一样收窄回去，但 Microsoft 是债务市场里成本最低的融资者之一。它的 TDS 交易在 55 个基点，相比之下 Oracle 在 325 个基点，而所有其他大盘投资级发行人则落在两者之间。

turns.en: So if Microsoft has to pay a little bit more, it pushes everybody else up, and so that's the kind of repricing that's going on, not the end of the world, a little bit of a signal.
turns.zh: 所以如果 Microsoft 都得付出多一点，它就会把其他所有人都往上推，这就是当下正在发生的那种重新定价——不是什么世界末日，只是一个小小的信号。

turns.en: And as we go forward, because I think we're early in earnings on this whole AI kind of conversation, which you're increasingly going to have Dom, which you're going to ask me a lot about every time I come back on, because now we're going to have transparency.
turns.zh: 随着我们往前走，因为我觉得关于整个 AI 这场对话，我们还处于盈利的早期——你会越来越多地、Dom——你会越来越频繁地问我这个，每次我回来上节目都会问，因为现在我们要迎来透明化了。

turns.en: Now we're going to have public bond prices, and we're going to have credit default swaps, that old tool from the GFC that people love to focus on, and we're going to have the ability to short it.
turns.zh: 现在我们会看到公开的债券价格，会看到信用违约互换（CDS）——那个从金融危机（GFC）时代留下来的老工具，人们总爱盯着它——我们还会拥有做空的可行性。

turns.en: We're going to have the ability to trade two-way in the credit markets, right? You can't do that in bank loans, you can't do that in private credit.
turns.zh: 我们会拥有在信用市场里双向交易的能力，对吧？这在银行贷款里做不到，在私募信贷里也做不到。

turns.en: Once you start going into the public bond markets, now you can do that, and now you get to see a little bit more price discovery, there'll be a lot more volatility.
turns.zh: 一旦你开始进入公开债券市场，现在你就能这么做了，现在你就能多看到一点价格发现，也会多出很多波动。

turns.en: Again, the volatility that we're seeing in Google stock, take note of it, that's a different region. It's outside the historical, we're all pulling up the historical Instagram, it's like, this thing isn't even on the chart, 12% down day and one day.
turns.zh: 再说一次，我们在 Google 股票上看到的那种波动，留意一下，那是一个不同的领域。它超出了历史区间——我们都在翻历史的图表，这东西根本就不在图里——一天跌 12%。

turns.en: And so we're moving into a different zip code, if you will, of market pricing, market volatility, market indigestion. It's not the end of the world, it's just a different phase of the AI build out.
turns.zh: 所以我们正在进入市场定价、市场波动、市场消化不良的一个不同区域（zip code），如果你这么说的话。这不是世界末日，只是 AI 建设进程中的一个不同阶段。

turns.en: You know, to your point about the kind of price transparency and kind of aspect of being in the public markets, one of the reasons why this is such a big deal is because over the course of the last year, we've watched bond insurance, credit default swaps, so to speak, for a company like Oracle, reach kind of like these historic high levels, the cost to insure against default, for even a company the size of Oracle is going up, up and away.
turns.zh: 呼应你关于价格透明、关于身处公开市场这一点——为什么这事这么重大的一个原因是，在过去这一年里，我们看着像 Oracle 这样公司的债券保险、或者说信用违约互换，冲到了历史高位，为违约做保险的成本——即便是 Oracle 这种规模的公司——也在一路上扬，越飘越高。

turns.en: We also saw something similar play out with regard to CoreWeave, a neocloud company, right? And it's bonds that have traded down in price so much that we were kind of pushing yields up to like this kind of 15, 17, 18, 19% range, I believe, don't quote me directly.
turns.zh: 我们还在新云公司 CoreWeave 身上看到了类似的情况，对吧？它的债券价格一路下挫，我想我们看着它的收益率被推到了大约 15%、17%、18%、19% 那个区间——具体别直接引我。

turns.en: But it was in the double digit teens, right, in terms of yield for CoreWeave, which at one point, not that long ago, was considered a Wall Street darling.
turns.zh: 但 CoreWeave 的收益率确实在双位数的十几，而它不久前还一度被视为华尔街的宠儿。

turns.en: So I wonder if you do have some of these types of pressures building up that are becoming more transparent, are we going to see maybe more speed and velocity in the way that markets move because there is a little bit more relative speed in understanding where price discovery is at?
turns.zh: 所以我想知道，如果确实有这类压力在不断积聚、又变得越来越透明，我们是否会在市场波动的速度和烈度上看到更多的变化，因为现在理解价格发现走到了哪一步，相对来说要快一点？

turns.en: I think back to the old bond trader saying, right, there are no such things as bad bonds, just bad prices, right, by the time it's done. So how does that play out?
turns.zh: 我想起老债券交易员常说的一句话：世上没有坏的债券，只有坏的价格，等这一切尘埃落定就是如此。那这会怎么展开呢？

turns.en: Yeah, so I think that's part of what I mean by like a new zip code for the AI trade. There's more price discovery, there's more price transparency, there's more ability for kind of the emotional swings between fear and greed to play out.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这正是我所说的 AI 交易进入一个新区域的一部分。这里有更多的价格发现、更多的价格透明度，也有更多空间让恐惧与贪婪之间那种情绪的摆动释放出来。

turns.en: I think about financial markets and these types of markets, big investment booms. They don't move in one direction, they ratchet. What I mean by ratchet is they go up, they reset, they go up again, they reset.
turns.zh: 我会去想金融市场、去想这类市场——大型投资热潮。它们不会只朝一个方向走，它们是棘轮式（ratchet）的。我说的棘轮是：往上走、重新校准、再往上走、再重新校准。

turns.en: We haven't really had as much of a ratchet up until now because it's been only one part, it's been just the positive part. Imagine what the narrative was a year ago, oh, this is great, it gives the hyperscalers something to do with their free cash flow, it gives them a return on investment, it was all positive, and as you move forward through it, it's still incredibly a positive story, but you start to get a little bit of the balance, you get a little bit of the AI pessimism or
turns.zh: 到此前我们其实没有太多棘轮式的表现，因为一直只有单面，只有正面的那一面。你想想一年前的叙事是怎样的：哦，这太好了，它让超大规模云厂商的自由现金流有了去处，给了它们一个投资回报，全都是正面的。而当你往下推进，这仍然是一个非常正面的故事，但你开始看到一点点平衡，开始看到一点点对 AI 的悲观、或者

turns.en: the naysayers or the negative view. I try to take a balanced view, I like to listen to both arguments, I think it's really, really impossible to know because ultimately the end state here is an unknowable state and that end state and we should all be very clear at what's at stake here is does the supply and the cost of the supply ultimately make or meet, I should restate this, does the demand and the price of the demand, price times quantity ultimately justify the incredible investment
turns.zh: 那些唱反调的人、那些负面的看法。我尽量保持一个平衡的视角，我喜欢听两边的论调。我觉得要真正知道是不可能的，因为归根到底，这里的终局是一个不可知的状态。而那个终局——我们都应该非常清楚这里面押着什么——是：供给和供给的成本，最终是否……我重新说一下……是需求和需求的价格，价格乘以数量，最终能否证明我们所做的这惊人的投资

turns.en: that we're making on the supply side and unfortunately we have to make that investment first before we can figure out the answer at the end and no one really knows.
turns.zh: 在供给侧的投资是合理的。而遗憾的是，我们必须先做出这份投资，才能到最后搞清楚答案，而没有人真正知道。

turns.en: Obviously everyone in making those investments believes that to be the case or you wouldn't make that investment, but there is another interesting counterargument that has to do with game theory that it's the overinvestment thesis that everybody ends up having to participate even if you don't know where the end state resides.
turns.zh: 显然，每一个做出这类投资的人都相信情况会如此，否则你不会去做那份投资。但还有另一个很有意思的反面论点，跟博弈论有关，就是过度投资论：每个人都不得不参与其中，哪怕你不知道终局在哪里。

turns.en: One point I want to clarify, you think about that CDS spread, don't think of it so much as the price of or the cost of default because long before you get to default, what's driving that re-pricing, it's really the price of the marginal access to capital.
turns.zh: 有一点我想澄清：你想到那个 CDS 利差时，别太把它当成违约的价格或违约的成本。因为在你走到违约那一步之前很久，真正驱动那番重新定价的，其实是边际获取资本的价格。

turns.en: That's really what the CDS market is telling you, especially because we're talking about CDS on the large cap IG hyperscalar names. The prospects there of default are very remote, but why you see that widening is because all those companies are trying to get access to more debt financing and when they get access or they ask for that access, it takes on counterparty risk, it takes on credit risk.
turns.zh: 这才是 CDS 市场真正在告诉你的，尤其是因为我们说的是那些大盘投资级、超大规模云厂商名字的 CDS。它们违约的可能性微乎其微。但你之所以看到利差走阔，是因为所有这些公司都在争取拿到更多债务融资，而当它们获得准入、或者去争取这份准入时，这就带上了对手方风险，带上了信用风险。

turns.en: What the CDS markets do is they help the banks, the intermediaries to offlay that counterparty risk that allows them to do those deals and do those transactions.
turns.zh: CDS 市场所做的，是帮助银行、帮助这些中介去转移那份对手方风险，从而让它们能够做成这些交易、完成这些操作。

turns.en: That's what you're now starting to see is that whatever innate capacity that I had to absorb, Microsoft, Google, counterparty risk, I've taken it all on.
turns.zh: 这就是你现在开始看到的：无论我原本有多少内在容量去吸收 Microsoft、Google 的对手方风险，我已经全部接下来了。

turns.en: It's all occupied. Now, I have to start laying that risk off. There's a story today about firms going to, I think it was a big bank, big European bank, going to insurance, saying, can we do a strategic risk transfer?
turns.zh: 全都占满了。现在，我不得不开始把这份风险往外转移。今天有一则报道，讲一些公司去找——我想是一家大银行，一家欧洲的银行——去找保险公司说：我们能不能做一次战略性的风险转移？

turns.en: Can we do a credit risk transfer type of agreement with insurance companies? You're going to see a lot of that as the size of this capital need needs to get dispersed throughout the financial industry as we have to find new ways of diversifying and spreading out the risk of the financing of this incredible capital expenditure that's required in order to bring about this incredible technology.
turns.zh: 我们能不能和保险公司做一个信用风险转移（credit risk transfer）类型的协议？你会看到越来越多这类事情，因为这份资本需求的规模需要被分散到整个金融行业里去——因为我们必须找到新的方式，去分散和摊薄这笔巨额资本开支融资的风险，而它为带来这项了不起的技术所必需。

turns.en: All right. One final question because I could go on for hours literally with you and I honestly could. In the last few moments that we have here, you mentioned the size and scope of just how much issuance is coming and what's going to be forecast to come down the pike.
turns.zh: 好。最后一个问题，因为我可以和你聊上几个小时，我是真的可以。在我们仅剩的这片刻里，你提到了这份即将到来的发行在规模和范围上有多庞大，以及接下来还会有多少被预测涌来。

turns.en: There are some folks that will make the argument that the types of money that we're talking about, the amounts and the size of it, are ones that could distort credit markets and rates markets.
turns.zh: 有些人会论证说，我们正在谈论的这类资金——它的量级和规模——是有能力扭曲信用市场和利率市场的。

turns.en: The biggest issuers out there are sovereigns, especially for the US Treasury market. Is there a point at which there is going to be so much debt capital that's needed to finance these aspirations for data centers and AI that we have, that you start to see some of the distortions play out even in the US Treasury market, which is the biggest, most liquid one in the world?
turns.zh: 最大的发行人在主权国家，尤其是对美国国债市场而言。会不会有那么一个临界点：为这些数据中心和 AI 的雄心所需融资的债务资本多到，你开始在甚至美国国债市场——这个全球最大、流动性最好的市场——里也看到一些扭曲显现？

turns.en: This is the competition for capital theme and I think it's very apt and I think it's very real and I think it's happening today. You have fundamentally in the private market, so non-governmentally related finance, you have a dramatic shift and that shift predates this conversation around data center financing and AI.
turns.zh: 这就是资本争夺（competition for capital）这个主题，我认为它非常贴切、非常真实，而且我认为此刻正在发生。从根本上说，在私募市场——也就是非政府相关的融资里——有一个戏剧性的转变，而这个转变早于我们这场关于数据中心融资和 AI 的讨论。

turns.en: It really was a post-COVID conversation where we started talking about the effects of reshoring and the impact on companies moving from just in time to just in case where the driving force wasn't margin and lowest cost producer, it was safest cost producer.
turns.zh: 它真的是一个后疫情（post-COVID）的对话：我们开始谈再在岸化（reshoring）的影响，谈企业从准时制（just in time）转向以防万一（just in case），驱动力不再是最优利润、最低成本生产商，而是最安全的成本生产商。

turns.en: That was starting to bring about some investment demand and it was a break from the pre-COVID period that we characterized by Larry Summers expression, secular stagnation.
turns.zh: 那开始带来一些投资需求，也是对我们称之为疫情前那段时期的一个断裂——用 Larry Summers 的话来说，那段时期叫长期停滞（secular stagnation）。

turns.en: That period was a period of excess savings and a lack of investment projects, a lack of investment demand. That drove down real interest rates, it drove down term premiums.
turns.zh: 那段时期是储蓄过剩、投资项目匮乏、投资需求不足的时期。它把实际利率压低，把期限溢价也压低。

turns.en: Now it's completely different and you add AI on top of that. Let's add some other things. You have the energy revolution, so you have climate, de-globalization, reshoring.
turns.zh: 而现在完全不同了，你还在其上叠加了 AI。我们再加几样东西：你有一场能源革命，所以有气候、去全球化、再在岸化。

turns.en: These are all major thematic expressions of new sources of demand for investment capital. On top of it, 2022, the chat GPT moment, we start the AI conversation.
turns.zh: 这些都是对投资资本新需求来源的重大主题性表达。而在此之上，2022 年，ChatGPT 的时刻，我们开启了 AI 这场对话。

turns.en: We didn't totally appreciate then how big of a capital expenditure this was going to be because initially the AIs were, they were little chatbots and we type into them and it might be 200 tokens.
turns.zh: 我们当时并没有完全领会这将会是一笔多么庞大的资本开支，因为最初的 AI 不过是些小聊天机器人，我们在里面打字，也许就是 200 个 token（词元）。

turns.en: What changed dramatically this year was the agentic revolution. We start interacting with AI, not typing in our little chatbot window, but as operating as agents doing very, very what we call long context windows, so long memory, highly sophisticated things, very sophisticated programming.
turns.zh: 今年戏剧性改变的是代理（agentic）革命。我们开始与 AI 互动——不再是往我们那个小聊天窗口里打字，而是让 AI 作为代理来运作，去做那些我们所说的长上下文窗口（long context windows）的事：超长记忆、高度复杂的东西、高度复杂的编程。

turns.en: Now you're talking about order of magnitude change in the amount of token usage, which then drives an order of magnitude change in the amount of token supply that is necessary.
turns.zh: 现在你要谈论的是 token 用量数量级的变化，而这又驱动了所需 token 供给数量级的变化。

turns.en: Now it just keeps on going, Dom. What's the latest view or change in the marginal source of demand? It was the meta release of Muse. Now we have a retail friendly, consumer friendly app where we can see this incredible use of agents, but now wrapped up in a very user friendly approach that we could see have incredible long tail consumer demand.
turns.zh: 然后它就一路停不下来，Dom。需求边际来源的最新变化是什么？是 Meta 发布的 Muse。现在我们有了一个面向零售、面向消费者的友好应用，我们能看到代理被如此惊人地使用，而且被包装在一种非常用户友好的方式里，我们可以看到它将带来惊人的长尾消费需求。

turns.en: It's not just codecs and code assistants and the versions of enterprise usage. We could see a consumer usage of this agentic future that increases demand.
turns.zh: 这不只是代码模型（codecs）和代码助手，以及企业级使用的各种版本。我们可以看到这种代理式未来的消费者级使用，它会增加需求。

turns.en: All of this is happening so, so quickly that it just is changing this calculus around how much capital are we going to have to spend to deliver this supply that's necessary to meet this incredible amount of demand.
turns.zh: 所有这一切发生得如此之快，它正在改变这样一个算计：我们要花多少资本，才能交付出满足这惊人需求量所必需的供给。

turns.en: It's a very fast moving equation, no one really knows, but clearly what we are seeing here is a shift outward in the investment demand curve and that in the environment where, what's the other big story, fiscally governments are in a more difficult position.
turns.zh: 这是一个移动得非常快的方程式，没有人真正知道。但显然，我们在这里看到的是投资需求曲线向外移动。而在这样一个环境里——另一个大故事是什么——各国政府在财政上处境更难。

turns.en: We saw that play out in France and the incredible widening in the France cost of borrowing. We see it in the projections of US debt and deficits, so we're running 6%, 7% deficit levels.
turns.zh: 我们看到这正在法国上演，法国的借贷成本出现了惊人的走阔。我们在美国的债务和赤字预测里也看得到——我们现在跑的是 6%、7% 的赤字水平。

turns.en: We used to be at 2 or 3, so it's a persistence of demand by countries also for that same debt capital financing and that is the competition for capital theme here.
turns.zh: 我们过去是在 2% 或 3%，所以各国对同一份债务资本融资的需求也在持续存在，这就是这里的资本争夺主题。

turns.en: And what does it mean? Again, it's not the end of the world, markets will clear. It's just at what price. And if you have more competition for capital, then the clearing price has to be higher, so that's the argument that real interest rates, they had a 40 year decline, now they're going to have a secular rise.
turns.zh: 那这意味着什么？再一次，这不是世界末日，市场会清算，只是以什么价格。如果你的资本竞争更激烈，那清算价格就得更高。所以这个论点就是：实际利率经历了四十年的下行，现在它们将迎来一场长期（secular）的上行。

turns.en: They don't necessarily shock upward, but they're going to be at a higher rate, so that real neutral rate that the Fed talks about, that's going to be higher.
turns.zh: 它们未必会骤然跳升，但会处在一个更高的水平。所以美联储谈到的那个实际中性利率，会更高。

turns.en: And then the term premium, how much more do you have to pay me as a bond investor to tie up my capital? Well, when there was an excess amount of supply of capital and not a lot of uses for it, that pushed the term premium down, so we had a 30 year decline in the term premium.
turns.zh: 然后是期限溢价：作为债券投资者，你要多付给我多少，才能把我的资本锁住？当初资本的供给过剩、用途又不多的时候，那把期限溢价压了下去，于是我们有了期限溢价三十年的下行。

turns.en: That term premium likely goes up over this time period as well and it just resets a lot of what the cost of capital is. And that is a lot of big macroeconomic impacts.
turns.zh: 在这个时期，期限溢价很可能同样会往上走，它会重置资本成本在很多方面的水准。而这对宏观经济有诸多重大的影响。

turns.en: The impact on AI is it's going to raise that marginal cost of capital. That's fine. The market will clear, but it will have some downstream impacts because as you raise the cost of that capital, you raise the overall cost of the supply side.
turns.zh: 对 AI 的影响是，它会抬高那份边际资本成本。那没关系，市场会清算。但它会有一些下游影响，因为你抬高了资本的成本，也就抬高了供给侧整体的成本。

turns.en: You need that demand ultimately to show up to make that equation work, makes that equation a little bit harder to work on the margin. Well, we're going to have to come back and revisit this the next time you're on because that whole narrative may be shifting around somewhat by the time we get back to you again.
turns.zh: 你最终需要那份需求显现出来，才能让这个方程式成立——它就在边际上让这个方程式更难成立一点。好吧，我们下次你上节目的时候得回来重新聊聊这个，因为等我们再接上你时，整个这套叙事可能都已经有所转变了。
